attacks.claim: The vendor tier cannot run the design. chain_poller needs ~160 req/min (320 with both expiries) and real-time quotes, but Starter allows 5 req/min with 15-min delayed quotes, so intraday triggers and 20 s repricing would act on stale data. Growth (100 req/min) is also too slow, and Growth + VPS = $259 breaches the $250 cap. The $139 cost figure rests on an unusable tier.
attacks.evidence: "40 underlyings => 160 requests/min during RTH." / "| Starter | $79 | 5 req/min | 15-min delayed |" / "We stay on Starter. Monthly run cost: Optiq Starter $79 + existing VPS $60 = $139"

attacks.claim: Migration 0042 runs in place on prod and drops roll_history in the same transaction as a 90-day-only backfill. There is no backup, snapshot, or down-migration, and older history is destroyed irreversibly, possibly breaking tax/audit needs.
attacks.evidence: "Migration 0042 runs in-place against prod Monday 08:00 ET" / "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history." / "older entries are not needed by roll_engine."

attacks.claim: The stated fallback conflicts with the migration. roll_eod.py is kept as the fallback through week 4, but the plan never confirms it does not read positions.roll_history, which is dropped on day one. If it does, rollback is broken.
attacks.evidence: "roll_eod.py stays deployed behind ROLLER_V2=false as the fallback path through week 4." vs "DROP COLUMN roll_history"

attacks.claim: The +3.8% net APR claim has no backtest or data, only anecdotal desk notes and a peer-practice argument. It then becomes the success criterion that gates rollout.
attacks.evidence: "Expected impact: +3.8% net APR vs. EOD rolling (see §2)." / "Desk notes ... 'would have been better'."

attacks.claim: Staleness and outage guards are incomplete. Only the broker heartbeat is checked; there is no quote-age or vendor-freshness check, no price sanity bounds on the mid-minus-1-tick limit, and nothing on what happens to in-flight combo orders or reprice loops on outage or kill.
attacks.evidence: "roll_engine stops emitting intents when the last successful broker heartbeat is > 60 s old." / ABSENT: snapshot age check and in-flight order handling

attacks.claim: Undefined behavior at the limits. When the 8-orders/day cap is hit or a combo is cancelled after 3 reprices, triggered deep-ITM short calls stay unrolled with no alert or fallback. There is also no in-flight lock against duplicate intents for the same contract while an order is working.
attacks.evidence: "max 8 roll orders per account per day" / "re-priced every 20 s up to 3 times, then cancelled." / "max 1 roll per contract per day"

attacks.claim: Paper mode compares intents with EOD decisions, not fill prices or P&L, and it runs on delayed data under the chosen tier. It cannot validate the claimed improvement before going live.
attacks.evidence: "paper mode (RollIntent written, no orders) alongside roll_eod.py; compare intents vs. EOD decisions daily."

attacks.claim: No alerting, 429/backoff handling, or partial-snapshot failure handling is specified for a 15 s polling loop across 40 underlyings. The all-or-none combo behavior is asserted without a source or test.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: alerting, 429 handling, runbook; "combo orders are all-or-none at the broker"
